body:
You are drafting spoken lines for a video game. Reply with plain text only, in the exact row format given at the end of this message. Do not send messages to anyone else and do not ask questions: decide. Write nothing but the rows (no title, no notes, no Markdown).

THE GAME. "The Crooked Moon" is a single-player, turn-based tactical party RPG built from a folk-horror Dungeons and Dragons campaign. It is set in Wickermoor Hollow, a haunted valley in Druskenvald, a land of endless night under a giant Crooked Moon with a crone's face. The look is a Halloween that never ends, drawn like an 1980s cartoon. A ghost train, the Ghostlight Express, has crashed in the valley; the party is stranded in the Hollow and its village, Wickermoor. The tone is warm, wry and funny on the surface, with real dread and real grief underneath. The player controls a party of four chosen from six companions: Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward, Silas Vane, Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein. They are quirky, capable adults.

THE NARRATOR. A NARRATOR row is spoken by the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of the ghost train, who tells the tale in a folksy Southern drawl. At the camp fire he is warm and wry, and when a talk turns sad his humour leaves and he goes plain and level. He speaks to the party as "you" and about the companion in the third person, by first name. Present tense, one or two sentences, under about 32 words. Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a touch, what the hands are doing) over adjectives. Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No facts the party could not see. Drop the final g ("hangin'") in about one Narrator row in four, and use no other dialect spelling. He is kind, never mocks a stumble and never makes light of the dead.

RULES FOR EVERY LINE.
1. The companion's voice sheet below comes first. Match its accent, pace, vocabulary and contractions, and the existing lines. Use a pet phrase at most twice in the whole reply and never twice in one talk. Never repeat or closely paraphrase a line already in the voice sheet or the note.
2. A SAY row is the companion speaking: one or two short sentences, under about 28 words. Never put three sentences in one row; start another row instead.
3. The party's options (OPTION rows) are under 12 words, in the plain voice of the party, work at any hour and in any weather, never name a hero, and are never rolls or checks. A reply must always answer the option it follows.
4. Canon limits. Use only the facts in the voice sheet and the note below. Do not invent a new named person, place, monster, event, object the companion carries, or piece of the companion's history. You may invent small, harmless habits, fondnesses, superstitions and turns of phrase, and the look of the fire and the night. Name no place that the note does not name. Never state a dark secret. You may come close to one and step back.
5. Nothing here is a game system: no dice, no checks, no points, no levels, no HP, no "approval", no menus talked about aloud. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks inside a line when someone is quoted). No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no asterisks, no stage directions, no placeholders.
6. Humour comes from the character, never explained. The sad turn is plain and short.
7. Our own words. Nothing quoted from any book.

THIS REQUEST. Region banter for The Crimson Monastery: 7 short exchanges between two or three companions, spoken as the party walks about this place. There are no Narrator rows, no options and no replies. Every row is a companion talking to another companion, never to the player.

HOW IT WORKS. When the party comes into an area, now and then one exchange plays as a few lines of chat between companions who happen to be in the party, once each. Only two or three of the six are ever in the party, so each exchange stands alone, mentions nobody else and needs no setup. Each one below is about what is in front of the party in one place at one moment of the story. Banter is funny first; one line in an exchange may turn honest, never more. The chat is about the place: what it looks and smells like, what is odd or sad or silly in it, and how each companion's trade, habits and fears meet it.

RULES.
1. Each exchange is 4 to 6 SAY rows, each a companion's single line (one or two short sentences, under about 28 words), alternating naturally between the speakers; every speaker listed speaks at least once.
2. Use only the facts in the attached cast sheets and the "In front of them" facts of that exchange. The "Story now" line is everything the party knows of the story: a remark must never run ahead of it (name a villain, a fight or a result only if the Story now line does). Never state or hint at any companion's past or secret, and never say what anyone's debt is. No new named people, places or monsters.
3. Pet words and phrases: each companion's at most once in an exchange, and never in two consecutive lines. Companions call each other by first name.
4. No two exchanges may share a joke or a topic, and no line may repeat a line in a cast sheet. Spread the topics: do not make every exchange about the same kind of thing.
5. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks). No em dashes, semicolons, brackets, asterisks or stage directions. No game terms. Our own words.
AVOID in this region: The belfry's bell and anything that rings in Delphine's memory is her own scene: nobody mentions the bell to her or about her. Do not describe Renathyr or the monastery's rulers. Do not give the monastery's history.

THE EXCHANGES (in this order):
EXCHANGE 1: Silas + Cordelia (speaker ids: silas_vane, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party has come inside the monastery's walls, on its peak.
  Talk about: its first look: what the party sees and smells on coming in.
  In front of them: The Crimson Monastery: A walled octagon on the peak: grounds, the Courtyard of the Rose, cloister halls, cells, a kitchen, a freezing larder and a domed cathedral. Spiked black walls, red glass in every window and a smell of iron and sulfur. Statues weep blood in the courtyard and the whole place is lit the colour of a wound. Parts of it: The monastery grounds; Jaeger's cabin; The Courtyard of the Rose; The monastery halls; The Sanguine Cathedral; The refectory; The monastic cells; The kitchen. Things to see: The Dead Larder; The altar, heaped with roses; The stone pulpit; The Bell Tower Gate; A butcher's worktable; A row of bare cells; A prayer nook over the valley; Hall doors with spikes on this side; A red-and-gold banner. People here: A gate veteran.
EXCHANGE 2: Rook + Tobin (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, tobin_hayward)
  Story now: The party has come up to the monastery's upper floor.
  In front of them: The Crimson Monastery, Upper Floor: A second ring of halls over the courtyard: the scriptorium, cells, and the priors' locked chambers. Red light through red glass. The scriptorium smells of ink and wax, and below the balustrade the courtyard waits. Parts of it: The scriptorium; The upper cells; Olaf's chambers; Cromwell's chambers; The upper halls; The east hall. Things to see: Lecterns of scripture; A balustrade over the courtyard; Beeswax candles, rendered from fat; Hunting trophies; A stained-glass window over the battlements; Blank books and paper; Calligrapher's tools; A bare cell.
EXCHANGE 3: Delphine + Lucan (speaker ids: delphine_ravelle, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The party is outside the east wall, at the Hunt's stables and kennels. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  In front of them: The Hunt's Stables and Kennels: Outside the east wall: the Hunt's warhorses, an armory shed, and bat hounds in boxes built into dead trees. Warm stink of horse and iron, and in the dead trees beyond, eyes that open when you pass. Parts of it: The stables; The armory; The kennels; The yard. Things to see: Hay; Saddles on a rack; A water trough; The Hunt's armory; A crate of bloody treats; A warhorse of the Hunt; A riding horse; A prisoners' wagon; A woodpile. People here: Landers; Marla; Fremont; A stable hand.
EXCHANGE 4: Delphine + Cordelia (speaker ids: delphine_ravelle, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party is climbing the monastery's bell tower.
  In front of them: The Bell Tower: Two floors of spiral stair, then a landing where bat hounds sleep, and a ladder to a trapdoor. Cold stone, a spiral stair, and the stink of wet dog and bat. Parts of it: The spiral stair; The landing. Things to see: A twenty-foot ladder to a trapdoor; Straw beds fouled by dogs; A slit window over the valley; Gnawed bones.
EXCHANGE 5: Rook + Silas (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, silas_vane)
  Story now: The party has reached the Bloody Sanctum.
  In front of them: The Bloody Sanctum: A vaulted chamber with a stone island and a round altar ringed by a moat of blood. A chandelier lights polished stone. The altar is etched with a rose and drowned in dried roses, and beside it lies a painting of an elf-woman. Parts of it: The blood channel; The stone island; The altar. Things to see: Father Renathyr at the altar; A journal on the altar; A painting of an elven woman; Dried roses, heaped; A chandelier of candles.
EXCHANGE 6: Lucan + Cordelia (speaker ids: lucan_houndstooth, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party is in the cathedral under a blood moon. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  In front of them: The Cathedral Under a Blood Moon: The cathedral on its side, altar east, blood on the floor and a red moon in the dome. Stained glass in red and violet, statues weeping, and through the dome a moon the colour of a wound. Parts of it: The cathedral; The altar. Things to see: Red and violet windows; A weeping statue.
EXCHANGE 7: Rook + Delphine (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: Renathyr is dead. The party is back in the monastery's grounds, which are quieter.
  Talk about: something different from the other exchange in this place: how it feels now.
  In front of them: The Crimson Monastery: A walled octagon on the peak: grounds, the Courtyard of the Rose, cloister halls, cells, a kitchen, a freezing larder and a domed cathedral. Spiked black walls, red glass in every window and a smell of iron and sulfur. Statues weep blood in the courtyard and the whole place is lit the colour of a wound. Parts of it: The monastery grounds; Jaeger's cabin; The Courtyard of the Rose; The monastery halls; The Sanguine Cathedral; The refectory; The monastic cells; The kitchen. Things to see: The Dead Larder; The altar, heaped with roses; The stone pulpit; The Bell Tower Gate; A butcher's worktable; A row of bare cells; A prayer nook over the valley; Hall doors with spikes on this side; A red-and-gold banner. People here: A gate veteran.

THE ROW FORMAT (exact). One row per line:

EXCHANGE <number>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
...

Use the speaker ids exactly as given (for example SAY rook_coldwake: ...). Write exactly 7 EXCHANGE blocks, numbered 1 to 7, and nothing else.

ATTACHED DOCUMENTS. Two documents come attached to this message; read both before you write: `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-1.md` (the voice sheets and fact lists for Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward and Silas Vane) and `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-2.md` (the same for Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein).
result:
EXCHANGE 1
SAY silas_vane: Spiked black walls, red glass in every window, and the air smells like a butcher's tab gone sour. I'd say the house is marking the deck, friend.
SAY cordelia_skein: Look at those courtyard statues, Silas, weeping fresh humours down the stonework without a single visible pump. The viscosity is a bit thin, though the sulfur masks it.
SAY silas_vane: And hall doors with the spikes pointed inward, so you know the management really trusts the regulars. Let me get this bitter herb censer swinging before my ribs stain pink.
SAY cordelia_skein: Do leave me an unspoiled drop off the stone pulpit first, darling. I have never run an assay on masonry that bleeds on command.
SAY silas_vane: Take a whole vial if you want, just don't ask me to double down on anything sitting in that Dead Larder.

EXCHANGE 2
SAY rook_coldwake: This balustrade over the courtyard is set square, Tobin, though the red glass ruins the light for proper ledger work. Too much glare on the docket.
SAY tobin_hayward: Never mind the glass, Rook, smell those candles by the lecterns. That is not honest hive-wax, that is tallow rendered from fat, and it is smoking foul.
SAY rook_coldwake: Aye, it leaves a greasy soot on the blank books and the masonry alike. Poor ventilation in the upper halls, and two chambers locked tight against inspection.
SAY tobin_hayward: Keep two paces between me and those wicks while we pass the scriptorium. I would rather chew fifty-year ink than let a fat-spark catch in my collar.
SAY rook_coldwake: Settle down now, I will walk on the candle side and keep the tower shield between the flame and your straw.

EXCHANGE 3
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Good heavens, Delphine, observe those boxes built into the dead trees beyond the yard. Bat hounds, if my nose has not lost its schooling in the horse-stink.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Charming accommodations, Lucan, though a crate of bloody treats is hardly top billing for the talent. Look at those little eyes opening in the bark like cheap seats.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Their kennel posture is terribly cramped, and I must deduct a full point for housing flying specimens above a prisoners' wagon. Barnaby is quite put out by the smell.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Your Foolishness just whispered a pun about barking up the wrong tree, and I am half tempted to throw him in the water trough.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Please restrain yourself, if you please, the warhorses are nervous enough with all this iron in the air.

EXCHANGE 4
SAY delphine_ravelle: Two floors of cold spiral stone and now a landing carpeted in fouled straw and gnawed bones. Mind the seams, darling, this staircase is a tragedy for velvet.
SAY cordelia_skein: My six eyes are dilating just looking at the bacterial culture in those dog beds, Delphine. One could harvest three distinct pathologies before reaching the twenty-foot ladder.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Keep your glass vials corked until we are through that trapdoor, because the stink of wet bat is already flattening my voice.
SAY cordelia_skein: Notice the draft coming through the slit window over the valley. It keeps the air cool enough that the marrow in those bones has barely begun to sour.
SAY delphine_ravelle: You have a crooked idea of a silver lining, Cordelia, now hold the rungs steady so I do not catch my hem.

EXCHANGE 5
SAY rook_coldwake: A round altar on a stone island, and a moat of open blood with no grating or drainage slope. That is a slip hazard and a gross violation of parish decency.
SAY silas_vane: Look at the stake they piled up, Rook, dried roses by the bushel and a chandelier burning like a high-roller's table. Tell's in the twitch, though, this whole room is a rig.
SAY rook_coldwake: There is a journal left open on the stone and a painting of an elven woman set right beside the channel. No proper clerk leaves paperwork inches from an unsealed trough.
SAY silas_vane: He painted her face like he was holding a winning hand and lost it on the turn of a single card.
SAY rook_coldwake: Mind the turf by the edge there, Silas, polished stone takes a slick film when the air is this damp.

EXCHANGE 6
SAY cordelia_skein: Fascinating pathology in this dome, Lucan, how the blood moon pours through the red and violet glass like a stained slide. Even the spilled humours on the floor look calibrated.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Hush now, the dark has teeth under a roof like this, Cordelia, and the scent of old iron is pressing rather hard behind my eyes. Keep your voice steady, if you please.
SAY cordelia_skein: Your pulse is climbing past a hundred, darling, though your diction remains admirably crisp. Shall I stand between you and the weeping statue while you take your notes?
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Thank you, yes, I would hate to let a feral snarl ruin my grading of the eastern altar's symmetry. Barnaby is already hiding behind my boots.

EXCHANGE 7
SAY delphine_ravelle: The house lights are still wound-red, Rook, and the roses on the altar haven't wilted an inch, yet the whole octagon feels like a hall after the curtain drops.
SAY rook_coldwake: The racket has gone out of the stonework, Delphine. My brass door-knocker hasn't given a single twitch since we came back through the courtyard.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Even the gate veteran looks like an usher waiting for someone to sweep up the programmes. I almost miss the tension, darling, it kept my stitching tight.
SAY rook_coldwake: Quiet is good for the mortar, even when the walls have spikes on the wrong side. I ought to remember to draw a breath before we clear the gate.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Take two, Rook, and I will pluck a dry rose off the stone pulpit for my lining before we leave the cheap seats behind.
